blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Burnaby total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Central Burnaby Condos and Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Central Burnaby's strata stock is a Norfolk Street cluster, not a town centre: the named complexes line Norfolk Street between Canada Way and Deer Lake Parkway, with one Canada Way frontage complex at Savile Row.

blocks.text: Central Burnaby Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: The rest of the Norfolk Street cluster is townhouse-form: Parkside Greene at 3888 Norfolk Street, Smith + Norfolk at 3868 Norfolk Street (16 townhomes, completed 2021) and Norfolk Terrace at 4025 Norfolk Street.
Savile Row at 5122–5152 Canada Way is the frame's Canada Way frontage townhouse strata, the only named complex on the arterial itself.

blocks.text: Central Burnaby Condos and Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Small Norfolk Street stratas are not exempt from depreciation reports: every British Columbia (BC) strata with five or more lots must obtain one on a five-year cycle since July 1, 2024, and only stratas of four or fewer lots are exempt.

A seven-unit self-managed strata, like the 3058 Smith Avenue complex in this frame, carries the same report duty: the provincial page makes no self-management exception for stratas of five or more lots.
Rezonings here proceed under the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026, the bylaw amended by the applications on the City's current Zoning Bylaw Amendments page.

blocks.text: Central Burnaby Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The 3058 Smith Avenue strata has only seven units and is self-managed, so council records, not a management company, hold its documents.
Winchelsea's two addresses, 3733 and 3738 Norfolk Street, face each other across Norfolk Street.
Savile Row's address is a range, 5122–5152 Canada Way, so a single unit's civic address may not match the complex name search.
Burnaby City Hall and the Deer Lake civic precinct sit at this frame's east end, beside Deer Lake Park, not inside a shopping district.

blocks.text: Central Burnaby Condos and Townhomes: costs and taxes

items.t: Utility notices in Burnaby are payable by the annual March due date for the discounted amount, and unpaid utility fees transfer to property taxes as arrears after December 31 — a strata owner's unit-level bill, separate from strata fees.

blocks.text: Central Burnaby Condos and Townhomes: getting around

items.t: Royal Oak Station on the Expo Line is this frame's SkyTrain access, named in TransLink's Expo Line station sequence between Metrotown and Edmonds.
Canada Way is the bus corridor for the Norfolk Street cluster, linking it east to the Deer Lake civic precinct and west toward Vancouver.

blocks.text: Central Burnaby Condos and Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Start with strata size: a Norfolk Street complex under five lots is exempt from the depreciation report duty, so the absence of a report at 3058 Smith Avenue's seven-unit neighbour complexes means different things by lot count — count the lots on the strata plan first.
Check the address, not the name, on Winchelsea documents: 3733 and 3738 Norfolk Street are separate stratas.

blocks.text: Central home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

9 townhomes sold in Central with a median price of $765,000 (the middle half sold between $745,000 and $802,000), taking a median of 17 days to sell at 98.7% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $725 per square foot, a median year built of 2011 and a median strata fee of $415 a month. 5 condos sold in Central with a median price of $575,000, taking a median of 27 days to sell at 96.0% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $619 per square foot, a median year built of 1993 and a median strata fee of $491 a month.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Central?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 10 condos and townhomes listed in Central. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Central a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In October 2026, condos and townhomes in Central had a sales ratio of not published for the month. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Central from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 4 condos and townhomes sold in Central over those 5 months, out of 916 in all of Burnaby.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did townhomes in Central sell for?
faq.a: 9 townhomes sold in Central between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $765,000.

faq.q: How long do townhomes take to sell in Central?
faq.a: The median was 17 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 98.7% of the last list price (0% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
